cells.tense: The drive is running close to what it tends and taking the yield in the same motion.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Before you improve anything, take something you have already made of what you tend and use it as it is, adding nothing, for as long as it holds your attention. Stop there.
cells.core:
The pull you feel toward what is growing is the same one that moves your work along, and here it is not straining. You see a green shoot or a rough draft and something quietly says not yet, so you turn to the next. That is not neglect; it is the drive keeping its own pace. The doing feels like itself, even when the doing is only watching.

Something that has already grown wants a sign from you. Before you improve anything, take something you have already made of what you tend and use it just as it is, adding nothing, for as long as it keeps you. Stop there. This is what the rhythm can feed next: abundant satisfaction, the imagined thing actually here, tasted before the next version starts.

cells.tense: Every possibility is being held open at once, for fear that one quiet corner means failure later.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Take what you tend whose next step is still being argued out in your head, and write that step as a single plain line. Then do that, or close the notebook on it.
cells.core:
You tend what is developing, and right now developing has become everything at once. Each one is still being pushed an inch forward, but the inch has stopped being enough. The future will not hold all of them open, and the effort to keep them that way is what empties the hours. It is not a failure of care.

Gather the scattered thoughts into one line. Take what you tend whose next step is still being argued out in your head — a plan, a piece, a bed — and write it as a single plain line. Then do that line tonight, or close the notebook on it and let the rest keep. This is what the rhythm can feed when the push is too spread to land: one view, one line, one day.

cells.tense: The bed is still there, but the hands that once answered what was planted are standing away.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Pick something you tend that changed while you were not pushing it, and name three things it already gave you. Then let it be.
cells.core:
Something you were tending has been left to its own course, and the drive has not moved to the next action. The tools are exactly where you put them, and the routine still runs, but you are not meeting what stands beside you — you are standing past a door as if the room behind it had closed. The care is steady. It has stopped expecting anything back.

Start with what you can count. Pick something that changed while you were not pushing it and name three things it already gave you. No plan for the next stage. Then let it be. This is what the rhythm can feed when the bed is hungry: endings honored, renewal trusted. What has grown is already sitting there; go and collect it.

cells.tense: The building is already in the hands; the work is steady, and the one doing it calls it nothing special.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Before anything else one day this week, name one part of what you are building — a single plain sentence, to nobody in particular — and do exactly that. No more.
cells.core:
You are keeping the conditions steady for something you tend, and the steadying is easy. The hours, the small repairs, the showing up — the care is already in your hands. But asked, you would say you are just doing what anyone would, because what gives the thing its shape is not being counted as yours. The commitment is there; the builder stands outside.

Before anything else one day this week, name one part of what you are building — a single plain sentence, to nobody in particular — and do exactly that. No more. That sentence is the whole of the acknowledging. Deep thresholds are crossed by work that is counted, not by work that hides. You are already the one building it.
cells.sheetLine: The care you give it already has a builder, and it is you.
